answer_text:
An isomorphism \(S_{20}\to S_{20}\) is an automorphism of \(S_{20}\).

For \(n\ge 3\) with \(n\ne 6\), every automorphism of \(S_n\) is inner. This holds in particular for \(n=20\). One way to see this is that an automorphism preserves order and centralizer sizes, and in \(S_{20}\) the transpositions are uniquely characterized among involutions by their centralizer size \(2\cdot 18!\). Thus an automorphism sends transpositions to transpositions, which forces it to be conjugation by some permutation in \(S_{20}\).

Since \(S_{20}\) has trivial center,

\[
\operatorname{Inn}(S_{20}) \cong S_{20},
\]

so the number of isomorphisms \(S_{20}\to S_{20}\) is

\[
|S_{20}| = 20!.
\]

\[
\boxed{20!}
\]
